name: Sībawayh
known: Abū Bishr ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān ibn Qanbar
summary: The Basran grammarian whose al-Kitāb, the first written grammar of Arabic, became the reference of every later book of naḥw and ṣarf.
bio: Sībawayh was of Persian origin and studied in Basra, above all with al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad. Reports differ on the details of his life; he died young, around 180/796, probably near Shiraz.
His one work has no title: later scholars simply call it al-Kitāb, the Book. It treats syntax, morphology and phonology in that order, and it was edited after his death by his student al-Akhfash.

works.title: al-Kitāb
works.note: The first comprehensive grammar of Arabic.
